# The first report has to cover tickets that predate it

Six tickets have delivered: SEEN-086, SEEN-087, SEEN-088, SEEN-093, SEEN-006, SEEN-094, SEEN-089 and
SEEN-090. None of them wrote a `kpi.json`, because the field did not exist until this ticket, and
SEEN-086 has no journal at all: it is the bootstrap, exempt by design.

So a report that reads `kpi.json` files would cover nothing at all this week, which would be a
reporting system whose first output is empty while eight tickets sit delivered in the tree. Three
decisions follow.

**The journal is the source, and kpi.json is a cache.** `harness report` derives every figure from the
journals themselves, exactly as `verify-delivery` will when it writes the file. A ticket delivered
before this ticket existed is therefore covered in full, and a ticket delivered after it is covered
identically whether or not its `kpi.json` is present. The file remains useful, because it is what a
later reader sees beside the receipt without recomputing anything, and because SEEN-091's own criteria
ask for it.

**A ticket with no journal is listed, not omitted.** SEEN-086 appears in the report with its points
and its delivery date from the ticket file, and every timing as `null`, with the reason named. A
report that quietly drops the one ticket that built the harness would be a poor first report.

**Delivered means the ticket's frontmatter says done or the journal holds a receipt.** SEEN-086 has
only the first, which is the whole reason the second cannot be the only test.
